To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the opossum renal cell line has a 5-HT1A receptor that is negatively coupled to the inhibition adenylyl cyclic AMP formation, that this receptor is down-regulated and desensitized by exposure to 5-HT, and that this desensitization is homologous.
the opossum 5-HT1b receptor is desensitized and down-regulated by 5-HT.

preincubation of cells expressing the 5-HT(1B) receptor with the receptor's agonist causes a decrease in the potency and efficacy of the functional response, and that the number of receptor binding sites is decreased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidation of the mechanisms involved in the regulation of the opossum 5-HT1 receptor.
the molecular mechanisms of 5-HT receptor function and dysfunction.
the regulation of the 5-Hydroxytryptamin (serotonin;5-HT)1b receptor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
5-HT1b receptor desensitization occurs via receptor phosphorylation and subsequent internalization.
the 5-HT receptor in the oopsum kidney cell line is desensitized and down-regulated by 5-HT.
desensitization and/or down-regulation of a G protein-coupled receptor is a function of the agonist, the cell type and the assay system used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the opossum 5-HT1A receptor is coupled to inhibition of adenylate cyclase via a G protein, that this G protein is a G(i) protein, and that the oposum kidney cell line 5-HT1b receptor is a member of the 5- HT1b family.
the 5-HT receptor is negatively coupled in the oposum kidney cell line to adenylylcyclase via a Gi/Go protein.

5-HT1A, 5-HT1D, and 5-HT1E receptors are negatively coupled to the adenylate cyclase pathway via a Gi protein, whereas 5-HT1F, 5-HT2, and 5HT4 receptors are positively coupled to the pathway via a Gs protein. 5-HT1, 5-HT3, 5-HT6, and 5-H7 receptors appear not to be coupled to the adenlylate cyclase pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 5-HT 1B receptor is a G-protein coupled receptor that is coupled to adenylic cyclase via a G-protein.
5-HT1 receptors are downregulated by chronic 5-HT exposure.
5-HT1 receptors are not only involved in the regulation of serotonin levels, but also in the regulation of the immune system.
